injuries.name: Hunter Henry
injuries.shortComment: Henry caught four of five targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Henry's seven-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter proved to be the game-winning score, putting New England ahead 23-16. After not finding the end zone the first four weeks of the season, Henry has scored in back-to-back games. The veteran tight end has been held under 50 yards receiving in five of six contests. He's the definition of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet ahead of Thursday's game with the Bears.

injuries.name: DeMario Douglas
injuries.shortComment: Douglas caught seven of eight targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets.
injuries.longComment: A.J. Brown returned to the lineup from his ankle injury and led the team with 10 targets, but he dropped multiple passes and finished with a 3-27-0 receiving line. After Romeo Doubs left with a shoulder injury early in the first half following a long touchdown grab, Douglas stepped into an increased offensive role. He ran 26 routes on Drake Maye's 35 dropbacks, and Douglas caught a nine-yard touchdown in the second quarter. He's posted back-to-back big box scores after logging 4-65-2 receiving last Sunday against Las Vegas. The Patriots' slot man doesn't have a big fantasy ceiling but looks like a passable WR4 during bye-week crunches headed into Thursday night's game against the Bears.

injuries.name: Morgan Moses
injuries.shortComment: Moses (ankle) was spotted wearing a walking boot after Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets, Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald reports.
injuries.longComment: After suffering an ankle injury in Sunday's meeting with the Jets, Moses didn't return. With the short turnaround for the Patriots ahead of Thursday's game against the Bears, the 35-year-old may not have time to recover and play. For now, Moses should at least be considered questionable, but if he can't suit up, Caleb Lomu may operate in his place.

injuries.name: Ben Brown
injuries.shortComment: Brown (knee) won't return to Sunday's game against the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Brown suffered a knee injury in the fourth quarter and has since been downgraded to out. Walter Rouse entered the contest and will presumably fill the void for the remainder of the game.

injuries.name: Alijah Vera-Tucker
injuries.shortComment: Vera-Tucker (hamstring) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Vera-Tucker sustained a hamstring injury in the second quarter of Sunday's contest. The left guard's absence has shifted the Patriots' offensive line around, leaving Ben Brown at left guard and Matt Pryor at right guard.

injuries.name: Romeo Doubs
injuries.shortComment: Doubs (shoulder) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Jets, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
injuries.longComment: Doubs was injured on his 42-yard TD catch in the first quarter, after which he went to the sideline tent, and eventually, the locker room. A shoulder issue was the cause for his exit and will keep him out for the rest of Week 6. A.J. Brown, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams are the Patriots' remaining healthy and available wide receivers.

injuries.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
injuries.shortComment: Stevenson will be joined by TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) in the backfield Sunday against the Jets, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: After Henderson suffered a right high-ankle sprain last Sunday versus the Raiders, Stevenson had a chance to take on a large workload in the short term, but with the former active, it's unclear if that's a possibility in Week 6. Any number of scenarios are possible for Henderson, from him taking on his normal number of touches to being available in an emergency capacity. Stevenson should be safe for roughly his typical 14.4 touches per game, which so far has amounted to 338 yards from scrimmage and two TDs in five contests this season.

injuries.name: Will Campbell
injuries.shortComment: Campbell (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Campbell sprained his right MCL in the Patriots' Week 5 win over the Raiders. The offensive tackle logged three limited practices during Week 6 prep and will attempt to play through the injury in Sunday's game.

injuries.name: Channing Canada
injuries.shortComment: Canada (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Canada will miss a third consecutive week due to a hamstring injury he suffered during Week 4 prep. The reserve option for the Patriots' secondary has an unclear return timeline but should have more grace due to the return of starting option Christian Gonzalez.

injuries.name: Behren Morton
injuries.shortComment: Morton (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Patriots' emergency third quarterback against the Jets on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Morton remains the third option at quarterback behind starter Drake Maye and backup Tommy DeVito. The seventh-round rookie will only enter Sunday's contest if both Maye and DeVito cannot return to the game.

injuries.name: TreVeyon Henderson
injuries.shortComment: Henderson (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Henderson emerged from a Week 5 win versus the Raiders with an apparent right high-ankle sprain, which typically requires a multi-week recovery. For this particular injury, though, he was able to log three consecutive limited practices this week, receive a questionable designation and then tell Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald on Friday that he's "hoping to play." Ian Rapoport of NFL Network then reported Sunday morning that Henderson was likely to suit up, which now has been confirmed. Even though he's active, the Patriots could lean more on Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner as the healthier options out of the backfield, but Henderson nonetheless has averaged 11 touches per game in his four appearances this season.

injuries.name: A.J. Brown
injuries.shortComment: Brown (ankle) is listed as active Sunday against the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Brown is making his first appearance since Week 1, when he suffered a right high-ankle sprain, and there's an expectation that he'll be able to play "a good amount" of snaps, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. What that may amount to for Brown remains to be seen, but in his 16 appearances (including playoffs) last season with the Eagles, he handled at least an 87 percent snap share in all but two of those contests.

injuries.name: Charles Woods
injuries.shortComment: Woods (shoulder) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Woods aggravated a shoulder injury in Week 5 against the Raiders, but he's been cleared to play Sunday after logging a full practice Friday. He has 22 tackles (16 solo) and three pass defenses through the first five games of the regular season.

injuries.name: Dre'Mont Jones
injuries.shortComment: Jones (shoulder) does not have an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Jones played through a shoulder injury in the Patriots' Week 5 win over the Raiders. The pass rusher logged 57 percent of the Patriots' defensive snaps in the game and will likely have a similar snap share in Week 6 against the Jets.

injuries.name: Christian Gonzalez
injuries.shortComment: Gonzalez (shoulder) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
injuries.longComment: Gonzalez missed the Patriots' last two games. He practiced in a limited capacity Wednesday. However, after being upgraded to a full participant Thursday, Gonzalez has the green light to suit up for the AFC East clash with the Jets on Sunday.

injuries.name: Marcus Bryant
injuries.shortComment: The Patriots opened the 21-day practice window Wednesday for Bryant (ankle) to return from injured reserve.
injuries.longComment: Bryant suffered an ankle injury in the preseason. The offensive tackle has served his regular-season, four-game minimum on IR and is ready to return to the field. Bryant was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, and the Patriots have until Nov. 4 to return him to the active roster, or he will finish the 2026 season on IR.
